validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE test applied: independent-source search plus a visual read of the sheet's own cited map (rule: a report cited for a pipeline is not unsupported until its MAPS are read, not just its text -- full-text pdftotext search of the EGAS Annual Report 2018/2019 PDF finds zero occurrences of 'Kima' anywhere in the 36-page extracted text, so a text-only search would wrongly flag this row; the actual support is visual). Two independent, non-GEM sources corroborate: (1) IPIC (an Egyptian pipeline EPC/fabrication contractor), whose own project-reference table at https://ipic-eg.com/projects/ lists, verbatim, under a '2016' year heading: 'GASCO | KIMA Aswan Fertalizers Gas P/L | 16" | 12.7/14.3 [mm wall] | X-60 | 4,000 [m]' -- i.e. GASCO (Egypt's national gas transmission company) as client, a dedicated 16-inch, 4,000 m (4.00 km) gas pipeline to the KIMA Aswan fertilizer plant, completed 2016. (2) KIMA's own official corporate site (kimaegypt.com, ProjectDetails.aspx?id=10) independently describes 'Project KIMA 2', a rehabilitation of the plant 'to work with natural gas technology' requiring '1,200,000 m3/day at 25 bar pressure' -- confirming from the END-USER side, with no reference to GEM/GASCO/IPIC, that KIMA underwent a real natural-gas conversion needing a dedicated high-pressure gas supply. (3) Visual corroboration from the GASCO national-grid map itself (EGAS Annual Report 2018/2019, printed page 35 = PDF page index 19 of the egyptoil-gas.com-hosted copy; rendered at 400 dpi and cropped for legibility): the map shows a distinct 'KIMA' industrial-complex icon (fertilizer-plant symbol) as its own node, fed by a short spur off the Kom Ombo-Aswan trunk near the 'Aswan' city node -- topologically consistent with StartLocation=Kima / State=Aswan. That map segment carries no printed diameter/length label of its own (see the spec entry below), so it corroborates LOCATION/EXISTENCE only, not the numeric values. Tier: high for existence (2 independent origins: an EPC contractor's project record and the end-user company's own site, neither derivable from the other or from GEM). Fuel=Gas and Status=operating both follow from the same IPIC entry (a 'Gas P/L' built for GASCO, completed 2016, with no evidence of decommissioning and an operating fertilizer plant still needing its gas feed as of 2026 per egyptoil-gas.com's current KIMA coverage, e.g. recent 'blue ammonia' production reporting). CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType=transmission is a reasonable fit given the tracker's only three options (transmission/gathering/distribution) -- this is a dedicated, GASCO-built, high-pressure industrial supply lateral off the national transmission grid, not a wellhead gathering line or a public distribution main, so I am not flagging it as a classification error despite its short length.

validity.researcher_notes: DUPLICATE watchlist question (P8072 'Kima Aswan Industrial', 4 km/16in, vs P8073 'Aswan-Kima', 20 km/24in): resolved NOT a duplicate. The GASCO national-grid map (EGAS AR2018/2019 p.35) shows these as two sequential, physically distinct segments of one delivery corridor rather than one line entered twice: a 24-inch, 20 km trunk spur running from the Kom Ombo mainline down to the 'Aswan' node (matches P8073's diameter+length essentially exactly), followed by a separate, shorter, smaller-diameter final lateral from that Aswan-area tie-in into the KIMA plant itself (16 in, 4 km per IPIC -- matches P8072). Per the batch's own duplicate heuristic, a same-corridor pair with DIFFERENT diameters (24in vs 16in) and different lengths (20km vs 4km) reads as two real, sequential segments, not a double-count of one physical pipe. The two rows' inverted naming ('Kima Aswan' vs 'Aswan-Kima' for what are actually two different, sequential pipes) is a plausible source of future confusion but not itself a data error requiring a merge.
